releases.body:
**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Added
- **A multilingual local model.** `provider: "local"` now also accepts
  `potion-multilingual-128M` (256 dimensions, 101 languages, MIT). It uses the
  same static scheme as the English default — no ONNX, no service, ~0.35 ms per
  chunk — and downloads its weights once (512 MB fp32, cached as 123 MB int8
  plus its tokenizer).

  Weights are quantized per token row. A single scale for the whole table was
  dominated by its largest value (5.7 against a mean of 0.25), so small rows
  rounded to zero: those rows ended up with a cosine of 0 against their fp32
  originals. Per-row scales keep every row above 0.9998 for 2 MB of extra
  scales.

  Measured with `bench/run.mjs`: English recall stays at 100% and MRR is 0.404
  against 0.490 for the English model and 0.518 for Mistral codestral; on five
  Spanish queries it is 0.433 against 0.500. The model does align the languages
  (cosine 0.69–0.77 between a Spanish question and its English translation,
  0.25 for unrelated text), but on this repository's English code the English
  model still ranks better. It is opt-in by model id because it holds ~500 MB
  while loaded; the process drops it after five idle minutes.

### Changed
- The benchmark set grows from 25 to 30 queries with five Spanish ones.

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Added
- **Bundled local embeddings: no API key and no network required.**
  `provider: "local"` embeds with a ~2 MB static model (potion-base-8M packed to
  128 dimensions at 4 bits) that runs in plain TypeScript in the same process —
  no native addon, no ONNX runtime, no background service — at about 0.2 ms per
  chunk. It becomes the default when no cloud credential is configured, so a
  fresh install indexes without any setup.

  Measured on this repository with `bench/run.mjs` (25 labelled queries):
  recall@10 stays at 100% and MRR moves from 0.518 (Mistral `codestral-embed`,
  1536 dimensions) to 0.490, while a full rebuild drops from ~2 minutes to
  ~6 seconds. The model is English-only: Spanish queries retrieve noticeably
  worse, and the cloud and Ollama providers remain for that case.

### Changed
- An unknown `provider` falls back by the same rule as the default: the bundled
  local model when there are no credentials, Mistral when there are.

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Changed
- **Verified against OpenCode 2.2 and OpenTUI 0.7.** OpenTUI 0.7 moves custom
  renderables onto construction-time hooks and replaces
  `defineNativeIntegration()`; this plugin uses neither, and its only OpenTUI
  surface — the JSX runtime (`jsx`/`jsxs`/`Fragment`) and
  `createTextAttributes` — is unchanged. The virtual module scheme the TUI
  relies on is unchanged in 2.2 as well, so there is no runtime change here:
  the development dependencies move to `@opentui/* 0.7` and the 2.2 SDK so the
  typecheck matches the host, and the optional peer ranges stay at `>=0.5.17`
  because both 0.6 and 0.7 work. Because `@opentui/*` are optional peers rather
  than dependencies, the new install-time requirement — plugins that pin
  OpenTUI 0.6 fail to install — does not apply.

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Changed
- **The TUI consumes the host's runtime instead of installing its own.** The
  terminal code imports the host singletons by virtual module id
  (`opentui:runtime-module:…`) and uses no JSX, and `solid-js`, `@opentui/core`
  and `@opentui/solid` are no longer installable dependencies (they remain dev
  dependencies and optional peers). A plugin installed from an npm spec used to
  load its own copies from `node_modules`, and the host never bridged the Solid
  runtime: the settings page and the footer indicator painted once and never
  updated — upstream
  [anomalyco/opencode#33884](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/33884).

### Added
- The settings page and the dialog menu show the plugin version, so a report
  about either names the build it came from.

### Fixed
- **Escape from the settings page returns to the session it was opened from**,
  instead of navigating to the home screen and losing the user's place.

### Documentation
- The README's *Requirements* no longer says the plugin installs ~14 MB of
  SolidJS/OpenTUI runtime; it states that the host provides those modules and
  the TUI consumes them by virtual module id.
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` moves `solid-js`, `@opentui/core` and
  `@opentui/solid` out of the distributed runtime dependencies: installing the
  package no longer brings copies of them.

Full history: https://github.com/Javierkaiser/opencode-indexing/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Changed
- `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` move to 0.6.6, and `@opencode/plugin`
  to 2.0.31 alongside them. That bump had been stuck: 0.6 was uninstallable
  on Node 22 while the JSX runtime was optional, because npm skips an
  optional dependency whose engine does not match. Declaring it as a real
  dependency is what let the install through, and the group now passes on
  all three platforms.
